title: Advanced Connectors
subtitle: Formal, written-style connectors for contrast, addition, and consequence.
objectives: Use whereas and despite/in spite of for formal contrast
Use nevertheless/consequently for formal consequence and contrast

content.intro: You already know but/so/because. This lesson gives you the more formal connectors used in essays, reports, and professional writing.

rules.heading: a) Contrast
rules.body:
• whereas (neutral contrast, joining two clauses): The north is mountainous, whereas the south is flat.
  • despite / in spite of + noun/gerund: Despite the rain, we went out. / In spite of losing, they stayed positive.
  • nevertheless (starts a new sentence): The plan was risky. Nevertheless, they went ahead.

rules.heading: b) Addition
rules.body: • furthermore / moreover (adds a stronger point, formal, starts a new sentence): The product is expensive. Furthermore, it's poorly made.

rules.heading: c) Consequence
rules.body: • consequently / as a result (formal result, starts a new sentence): Sales fell sharply. Consequently, the company cut costs.

examples: The north is mountainous, whereas the south is flat.
Despite the rain, we went out.
The plan was risky. Nevertheless, they went ahead.
The product is expensive. Furthermore, it's poorly made.
Sales fell sharply. Consequently, the company cut costs.
In spite of losing, the team stayed positive.

commonMistakes.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
commonMistakes.right: Despite the fact that it was raining, we went out. / Despite the rain, we went out.
commonMistakes.why: "Despite" takes a noun or gerund, not a full clause directly.

commonMistakes.wrong: The plan was risky, nevertheless they went ahead.
commonMistakes.right: The plan was risky. Nevertheless, they went ahead.
commonMistakes.why: "Nevertheless" typically starts a new sentence, with a period before it, not a comma joining one sentence.

commonMistakes.wrong: The report is late, furthermore is incomplete.
commonMistakes.right: The report is late. Furthermore, it is incomplete.
commonMistakes.why: "Furthermore" needs its own clause with a subject ("it"), not a fragment.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best formal connector.

items.prompt: The coffee here is excellent, ___ the tea is rather weak.
items.explanation: A neutral contrast between two facts — "whereas."

items.prompt: ___ the criticism, the director refused to change the ending.
Sales fell sharply. ___, the company cut costs.
The hotel was overpriced. ___, the service was poor.
items.explanation: A formal addition of a further, stronger point.

items.prompt: "The team lost the match. ___, they remained positive."
items.explanation: A contrast between the loss and their attitude — "nevertheless."

options: Despite he was tired, he finished the race.
Despite being tired, he finished the race.
Despite tired, he finished the race.
items.explanation: "Despite" needs a noun or gerund (being tired), not a full clause or bare adjective.

items.incorrect: Despite he arrived late, no one minded.
answer: Despite arriving late, no one minded.
Although he arrived late, no one minded.
items.explanation: "Despite" needs a noun/gerund, not a subject + verb clause.

items.incorrect: The report was late, nevertheless it was accurate.
answer: The report was late. Nevertheless, it was accurate.

summary: Whereas = neutral contrast joining two clauses. Despite/in spite of + noun/gerund = contrast.
Furthermore/moreover = formal addition. Nevertheless = formal contrast, new sentence.
Consequently/as a result = formal consequence, new sentence.
